final.label: test-name-tag-output-conventions

skill_entry.name: 5. A test's name, tag list and result print agree with its assertions and with the file's convention
skill_entry.trigger: Any one. (A) Name: the diff adds, removes or rewrites an assertion, a comment or the stimulus inside a TEST_CASE or SECTION, or a comment inside the unit flips a verb (preserve/zero, keep/drop, accept/reject) while the name keeps the old verb. Re-spelling an expression inside an existing call or assertion, or moving a comment with its words unchanged, does not trigger. (B) Tag: the diff adds a test unit whose name and tag string are not both present at BASE in that file, every pre-existing unit of the file shares one tag count, and the new unit's tag count differs or one of its tags is not spelled from its name. (C) Print: the diff adds an unguarded counter print followed within three lines by a REQUIRE or CHECK of that counter against zero, in a file where at least one sibling summary print of that counter kind exists and every such print is guarded.
skill_entry.procedure: Iterate per unit, never per hunk. (A) Extract the verb and object from the name; read the setup; for each assertion that observes the object write 'fails when <state>'; the name must describe the passing state and agree with the verbs of the unit's own comments; grep the name in the file header comment and the PR body for rename sites. A new unit with no assertion stops with a one-line note. (B) Tabulate (macro, name, tags) for the whole file at HEAD, split multi-tag strings, mark the new units; convention = the tag count every pre-existing unit shares, with tags spelled from the name; candidate = a new unit that breaks it. (C) List the new unit's counter prints and the sibling summary prints with the line above each; drop per-element prints. Report A, B and C as separate nits.
skill_entry.question: Test label: reading the unit's name, tag string or result print next to the setup, the REQUIRE lines and the sibling units of the same file, does the label describe the state in which the assertions pass, and does it follow the pattern the siblings already use?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: (A) a topic label without a verb; a name wrong on main in a unit the diff touches only by re-spellings (note once); an assertion the name does not mention. (B) a pre-existing unit's tag (`[direct_rw_one]`, `[attention_command_Output_validation]`); a plain TEST_CASE among TEST_CASE_METHOD siblings whose single tag is spelled from its name (`[dma_xfer_state]`); a hidden `[.name]`; a moved unit; a new file; a file whose pre-existing units share no tag count or use shared topic tags (t_llama_unit.cpp `[kv_data]`). (C) a print with no REQUIRE on that counter (the per-fetcher print, PR 1666); a file whose sibling prints are unconditional (t_hwattention_replay.cpp); a print inside a helper that returns a bool; the log level; indentation. A hidden-tag flip is check 3; a label outside a Catch2 tag string is the identifier-name check; a comment against code lines is the comment-versus-code check.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A) "Nit: the section is still named '<name>', but it now asserts that <opposite state> (REQUIRE at :<line>; the comment at :<line> says '<new verb>')." (B) a suggestion block with the tag spelled from the name, then: "maybe? Or... is/was the intention to start grouping a subset of these tests under the `[<tag>]` category (which makes sense too)? It's just that this is the only test using that atm..." (C) a suggestion block `if (<count>) <print>;` then: "... in the other tests, this is only printed if there were actually mismatches found. Should be consistent?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit for A (he writes "Nit:"); B is a suggestion block followed by "maybe?" with no severity word, read here as a nit; C is a suggestion block ending in a question ("Should be consistent?"), minor. Never blocking: the authors changed the code within two hours (PR 1666: 5e0bc3f788 at 18:05Z after the 17:20Z comment; PR 2078: f0134b976b at 17:48Z after 16:01Z) or the same local day (PR 4557: c5d44bd86f 2026-10-05 21:52 -0700 after the 20:18Z comment).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk plus the full test file at HEAD (sibling declarations, tags and print guards) and the same file at BASE (moved-unit test); file header comment and PR body for rename sites; commit messages only if the PR will not be squashed; `gh api pulls/comments/<id>` for original_commit_id when a comment's commit differs from the review's commit.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 5: a test's name, tag list and result print agree with its assertions and with the file's convention

Setup note. If `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself (a merged PR reviewed at a historical head) or the PR's base_ref is not main, take BASE from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/commits --jq '.[0].parents[0].sha'`. On PR 2078: BASE = be689b7251, HEAD = 9d64b4a8bf (merge-base against origin/hwattention_sync returns HEAD; against origin/main returns b0df78db3c, which is wrong). When a comment's commit differs from the review's commit, anchor at `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> -q '.original_commit_id,.original_line'`.

1. Hunks: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' 't/*.hpp' | grep -n '^+++\|^@@\|^[-+]'`. Drop a hunk that only re-spells an expression inside an existing call or assertion (an argument, an index such as `queues[0]` to `queues[process_device_id{0}]`, a type wrapper) or moves a comment without changing its words: it adds no assertion and changes no statement about the code under test. New units: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' | grep -o -E '^\+ *(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(.*'`, then the HEAD line of each with `grep -n -F '<name>' full/<file>`. Moved-unit test: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -c -F '"<name>"'`; a unit whose name and tag string both exist at BASE is moved, not new. A hunk is only a container: run the rest per unit (every new unit, plus every pre-existing unit whose body a kept hunk changes).
2. Enclosing unit of a changed line L in a pre-existing unit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<L> '/^(TEST_CASE|TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(/ {t=NR; name=$0; s=0} /^  SECTION\(/ {s=NR; sn=$0} /^  }$/ {if (s) s=0} NR==L {print (s? s": "sn : t": "name); exit}'` (a SECTION at two-space indent closes at the next `  }` at that indent). A line above the first TEST_CASE stops here.
3. (A) Extract the name's verb and object. A new unit with no REQUIRE or CHECK stops here with the note "no assertion, name not judged by this check".
4. Read the setup lines that put the object into its pre-call state.
5. For every assertion that observes the object, directly or through a value computed from it (follow the read path), write "fails when <state>". Skip assertions that pin a write's partner invariant.
6. The name must describe the passing state and agree with the verbs of the unit's own comments. Comment flip in a changed unit: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- <file> | grep -n '^@@\|^[-+] *//'`, keeping comment lines under a `@@` whose new-side start lies inside the unit. A new unit has no old comment to flip: compare the name verb with `awk -v S=<S> -v E=<E> 'NR>=S && NR<=E' full/<file> | grep -n '//'` and stop when they agree.
7. Rename sites: `grep -n '<name>' full/<file>` and the PR body; commit messages only if the PR will not be squashed. List them inside the one finding.
8. (B) Table of the whole file at HEAD, multi-line declarations flattened: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E '(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\([^{]*\{' | sed 's/ \+/ /g'`. Declaration lines: `grep -n -E '^(TEST_CASE|TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(' full/<file>`. Per-tag membership with multi-tag strings split: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E '(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\([^{]*\{' | grep -o -E '"\[[^"]*\]"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/\]\[/\n/g; s/[][]//g; s/^\.//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. Record per unit: new or pre-existing (step 1), tag count, and for each tag whether it is spelled from the name. Definition: a tag is spelled from the name when every word of the tag (split on `_`, leading `.` removed, case folded) equals a word of the name (split on `_` and space) or is a prefix of one (`poly` for `polymorphic`). Convention: the tag count that every pre-existing unit shares, and tags spelled from the name in all but at most one pre-existing unit. If the pre-existing units share no tag count, or their tags are topic tags shared by several units (t/t_llama_unit.cpp: `[kv_data]` has 12 members at a9a9cf30a4; t/t_hwattention_2.cpp mixes one-, two- and three-tag units at 05b6ac0549), the file has no convention and (B) stops. Candidate = a new unit whose tag count differs from the shared count, or any of whose tags is not spelled from its name. "A tag no sibling uses" is not a discriminator in a file where every tag has one member; keep it only as the wording of the question to the author.
9. (C) Unit range: S = the declaration line, E = the next declaration line minus 1 (end of file for the last unit). Counter prints only: `awk -v S=<S> -v E=<E> 'NR>=S && NR<=E' full/<file> | grep -n -A3 -E 'spdlog::(info|warn|error)\(' | grep -B3 -E '(REQUIRE|CHECK)\(.*== *0\)'`; keep a print only when the counter in its argument list is the one the REQUIRE compares. Banner and progress prints (no counter argument) are dropped without reading context. For each kept print record whether the preceding non-blank line is an `if (` whose condition names the counter.
10. Sibling summary prints of the same counter kind: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -B1 -E 'spdlog::(info|warn|error)\(".*(found|overall)'`; drop any hit whose preceding line is `++<counter>;` or that prints a per-element index (`K mismatch (head {}, idx {})`, b0e53be7e0:561, :592, :708, :739). A guard is any `if (` on the preceding non-blank line whose condition names the counter, including `if (a || b)` (9d64b4a8bf:1308) and `if (count > 0)`. (C) fires only when at least one sibling summary print exists, every one is guarded, and the new one is not; the finding is a suggestion block adding the guard in the siblings' spelling. Do not comment on the log level or on indentation.
11. Report A, B and C as separate nits anchored at the name, the macro line and the print line.

On PR 4557 (A), BASE e5fa372c19, HEAD 96a6220ab6: SECTION "append_v preserves poison" (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3293, inside TEST_CASE "scaled_v padding NaN" at :3278); stimulus GENERATE at :3298; comment flip: BASE "will preserve this NaN" to HEAD :3325 "must zero this NaN"; assertion REQUIRE_FALSE(std::isnan) at :3385 observes token 7 through scaled_v (call at :3377); rename sites: header comment :3273, commit 707159b9ef. Renamed at c5d44bd86f:3275 to "append_v zeroes the poisoned partner", header comment :3255. Pre-existing units touched only by v_source_row re-spellings (:684, :1849 and eight more) do not trigger.

On PR 2078 (B), BASE be689b7251, HEAD 9d64b4a8bf, executed 2026-10-06: one t/ hunk of 426 added lines (`@@ -1491,0 +1492,426 @@`) holding 5 new units (:1493, :1560, :1624, :1787, :1869); t/t_hwattention.cpp has 13 units, 8 pre-existing (:97, :115, :179, :256, :329, :500, :659, :1444-1445 two-line declaration). All 11 TEST_CASE_METHOD units carry one tag; 9 spell it from the name, :659 is the hidden `[.stream_k_and_v]`, the pre-existing :97 carries `[direct_rw_one]` for "single_value_write_read_direct". Every tag has exactly one member after splitting (14 tags). Convention: 1 tag, spelled from the name (7 of 8 pre-existing). Candidate :1787 `TEST_CASE("polymorphic cacheblock xfer", "[hwattention][pos]")` (2 tags, neither spelled from the name): fires. :1869 `TEST_CASE("dma_xfer_state comparison", "[dma_xfer_state]")` (1 tag from the name, plain TEST_CASE): does not fire; Wade did not comment. (A) 13 assertions in 4 new units, 0 findings; :1787-1868 has no assertion. (C) 2 counter prints (:1747, :1776), both guarded, 0 findings. Fixed at f0134b976b:1789 `TEST_CASE("polymorphic hwcacheblock xfer", "[poly_hwcacheblock_xfer]")`.

On PR 1666 (C), reviewed state b0e53be7e0 (comment 2620236334 was posted in review 3579335328 at 2025-12-15T17:20:30Z; GitHub reports original_commit_id b0e53be7e0, original_line 1376; the corpus commit c5fd3de93b / line 1377 is GitHub's moved anchor after 5e0bc3f788 inserted the guard; line numbers coincide up to :1375): new unit TEST_CASE_METHOD(fixture, "attention_command_output_validation", "[attention_command_Output_validation]") at :1262-1264. The print at :1376 `spdlog::info("Found {} k mismatches and {} v mismatches overall", k_mm, v_mm);` has `}` above it and `REQUIRE(k_mm == 0)` at :1377. Sibling summary prints :567, :597, :714, :744 each sit under `if (mismatch_count > 0) {` (level error): fires. The per-fetcher print at :1367-1368 has no REQUIRE on fk_mm/fv_mm and does not fire. The tag's capital O does not fire. Fixed by 5e0bc3f788 "Update t/t_hwattention.cpp" (1 insertion: `if (k_mm || v_mm)` at column 0), visible at c5fd3de93b:1376-1377.
